description:
From the fz-kdt.183 rule review (2026-09-03, attacks-r2/g0n.fz, g0_direct.fz):
a mutually-recursive step/cont pair modelled on the library's own protocol.
Under 183's demand-through-forwarding rule step/2's LIST slot grounds
correctly ([{:cont, list(a0_1_e)}, list(binary)] and [.., list(int)] split),
but its {:done, acc} slot is masked TupleFields({0: Whole}) -- the tag only --
while the body's RETURN is acc, field 1, which the key erases. Both users
reach the one {:done, list(a0_1_e)}, empty_list() activation and its joined
return blends [binary] | [int]; g0_direct.fz fails identically at base and
under the rule. It does not fire in the library only because
Enum.reduce_finish/1 is NON-recursive (its key carries evidence). The class
is neither fz-kdt.183's element axis nor fz-kdt.165's callable axis: demand
that reaches a RETURNED tuple field. 183's invariant ("an activation's
published return may depend only on what its key names") is therefore a
structural over-approximation fitting the library's shape, not a proof --
183's text says so now. Direction: the same demand derivation, with "the
body returns this position (or a projection of it)" as a demand source
beside clause selection and forwarding -- i.e. return-flow demand on the
input-demand fact (InputDemand gains a `returned` axis or the forwarded axis
learns to see the return). Red-first: g0n.fz keys two {:done, ..}
activations and g0_direct.fz prints each user's own list on three doors.
CONCORDANT: fz-kdt.183 (the derivation to extend), fz-kdt.165 (the callable
axis on the same walk), fz-kdt.190 (a joined return published as a fact).

comments.text: fz-kdt.183 landed (2e0bb2706): unblocked. Reproducer: step/2 with a {:done, acc} slot keyed TupleFields({0: Whole}) -- the key names the tag while the return IS acc. The forwarding rule does not touch it; it fires in the library only because Enum.reduce_finish/1 is non-recursive. (The source is in the 183 research artifacts as g0n.fz; reconstruct from this description.)

A SECOND, SHARPER REPRODUCER and a corpus consequence, from the fz-kdt.120 re-cut research (2026-09-03, ca23b676f). Your shape is what blocks fz-kdt.120. Enum.reduce/3 finishes through `reduce_finish({:done, a} | ..) :: a`. The first ascent rung's argument is `{:done, []}`, and because the tuple FIELD is freight (masked TupleFields({0: Whole}), keying the tag only) while the return IS that field, `a` binds `[]` and the join-only ladder never re-narrows -- Enum.reverse/1([int]) types as `[]`. Measured consequence: the fz-f98.16 empty-list cleaner in arrow_match.rs is the only thing discarding that stale binding today. Delete the cleaner (which fz-kdt.120 must do, and which fz-kdt.184 deliberately left inert for it) and SEVEN corpus fixtures produce WRONG ANSWERS -- 00276, 00277, 00420, enum_map_family, enum_take_drop_split, fz_f98_range_map_converges, mailbox_closure_enum_hofs -- with Enum.map/to_list/with_index collapsing to []. So this ticket is not only a precision matter: it is load-bearing for correctness the moment the masking cleaner goes. fz-kdt.120 is now marked BLOCKED BY this ticket. Red-first for you should include: with the acc field keyed, `Enum.reverse/1([int])` types as [int] and not [], and the seven fixtures stay correct with the cleaner deleted.

CORRECTION FROM MEASUREMENT -- my earlier comment on this ticket was wrong, and the coordinator withdraws it. I claimed this ticket was fz-kdt.120's blocker, inferring it from the shape of the {:done, acc} rung. The fz-kdt.199 research measured it stacked and REFUTED that: with this ticket's rule applied AND the empty-list cleaner deleted, all seven fixtures still move and Enum.reverse/1([int]) still types as []. The wrong return sits on List.reduce_cont/3[list(int), empty_list(), a2] -- a key with NOTHING collapsed -- so no keying rule can reach it. The real blocker is fz-kdt.210 (a ground seed instantiating a @spec return variable, which refine_call_return then meets into the published return). The `fz-kdt.199 blocks fz-kdt.120` dependency has been removed.

THIS TICKET STANDS ON ITS OWN, and is wider than its body says. Measured at ca23b676f: `walk({:go, acc}, n)` keys G.walk/2[{:go, list(a0_1_e)}, int] -- field 1 is the address var, the local mask is TupleFields({0: Whole}), and forwarded_inputs finds NO forward edge at all (both self-calls hand slot 0 a Tuple CONSTRUCTION, opaque under fz-kdt.183's rule). That one key publishes non_empty_list(binary) | non_empty_list(int), and a @spec strings([binary]) consumer turns it into error[spec/violation] ([binary] | [int]) -- a real wrong diagnostic on a legitimate program. AND: `loop(0, junk), do: junk` -- fz-kdt.183's OWN first keying law, blessed as "freight must key ONE activation" -- has the identical defect at base. So that law is a COST pin, not a correctness one, and this ticket is what makes it safe.

title: A returned tuple FIELD at a recursive key is freight: a {:done, acc} slot masked TupleFields({0: Whole}) keys only the tag while the return IS acc, so two users still share one joined return
